sources.entry: invoke - A tool for managing shell-oriented subprocesses and organizing executable Python code into CLI-invokable tasks.

summary.one_liner: Invoke is a Python library for running shell-oriented subprocesses and organizing Python code into CLI-invokable tasks.
summary.what_it_does: Invoke is a Python library for managing shell-oriented subprocesses and organizing executable Python code into CLI-invokable tasks. The README says it draws inspiration from make/rake and Fabric 1.x. The README itself is short and points to external resources for a high-level introduction with example code, and for detailed API docs. It also links to a changelog and a maintainer roadmap. The README does not list specific features beyond the one-line description, so details on the task API or subprocess handling are not confirmed here.
use_cases: running shell commands from Python code
building command-line task runners for Python projects
notable: Organizes Python functions into CLI-invokable tasks
Takes inspiration from make/rake and Fabric 1.x
Project website and versioned API docs linked from README
caveats: README is brief and defers examples and API details to external docs
License not stated in the README provided
